about: Allele-identity cases. Each pairs a database record of a variant with what a subject's data holds at that position, and says whether the subject should be counted as a carrier. Coordinates, ids and letters are synthetic and do not describe any real variant or person.

cases.why: The record is an indel (AA>C). An array reports two letters, A and C, which also fit a plain SNP. A C in the genotype does not make the subject a carrier of the indel.
The subject carries C. The record's alternate allele is A, so this is a different variant at the same position.
The data row's own alternate allele is A and the record's is T. Same position, different variant.
T is neither the record's reference A nor its alternate G. The genotype is not drawn from the record's alleles, so it is not evidence for A>G.
Both are one-base deletions at the same position, but they delete different bases: A in the record, T in the data row.
An exact SNV match: one copy of the record's alternate allele, the other copy reference.
Two copies of the record's alternate allele.
The data row's reference and alternate alleles equal the record's, and the genotype carries the alternate.
The same one-base deletion written with a longer anchor (CAA>CA instead of CA>C). Comparing the letters misses it; comparing minimal representations matches it.
